MY GROK BOT REJECTED 147 MEMECOINS WHILE I WAS ASLEEP

The 6 it actually bought turned my last $285 into $7,438.62 overnight

And I didn't make a single trade myself

A week ago, my bot was basically gambling

It would see a green candle, read some bullish posts on X, and convince itself that every new token was the next 100x

So I changed one thing

I stopped asking Grok which coins would pump

Instead, I connected it to XERJ Reader and made it investigate every token before spending a dollar

Every potential entry had to pass 4 checks:

> SCOUT: Are new buyers actually increasing?
> HOLDERS: Are the top wallets accumulating or dumping?
> DEV: Is the deployer still holding a suspicious amount?
> SOCIAL: Is there a real launch announcement on X?

If XERJ couldn't find evidence for even one critical answer, the bot had one instruction:

REJECTED. NO TRADE.

At 2:17 AM, it rejected a token that was already up 340%

The reason? It couldn't verify the developer's wallet activity

That token collapsed 89% less than an hour later

Meanwhile, my bot quietly executed 6 trades on Fomo

https://t.co/t5AySrOof1

5 winners, 1 loser

The biggest winner alone brought in over $4,100

When I checked my wallet in the morning:

$285 → $7,438.62

And here's what surprised me most

All those XERJ Reader checks cost me just a few cents

I spent more on coffee yesterday than my entire AI trading desk spent reading data all night

I used to think the secret was finding the next 100x before everyone else

Turns out, sometimes the real edge is having a bot that knows when NOT to buy

Now I'm wondering what happens if I let it run for 30 days

Skills in Grok Bot

Once a task works the way you want, you can save the whole process as a skill

It keeps:
- steps
- rules
- output format
- things that need your approval

after that any of your bots can call it by name instead of reinventing the process each time

you can also teach a skill by doing the task yourself once on the bot’s computer

it records what you did and turns it into something reusable

It’s the difference between getting lucky with a good result and actually keeping it
